audit.why: 54.06% over 1058 games and the page reads FAV / 4/10 with carry threat 5/10. The lane shape on the page — Sett bullies levels 1-5, Purgatory evens 6 through first item, Sett retakes it at two-plus items — matches the packet chart exactly.
audit.corrected: FAV, difficulty 4/10. Only levels 6 and first item are genuinely even.

audit.why: Both layers already read Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Skill / Sett, identical to the packet levelChart, and each why names the same owner as its token. No mirror exists for this matchup yet, so this page sets the reference.
audit.corrected: Chart left unchanged; it is already consistent across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page describes the interactions well but names no cooldown for anything except E's ten seconds — the packet's only defect is 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Ashen Pursuit's auto-attack reset is also unstated, so the reader watches for a cast when the wind-up is the tell.
audit.why: From the kit: Q 10s at rank 1 down to 6s, 950 range. W 18s at rank 1 down to 14s. E flat 10s at every rank, 425 range, flagged both dash and autoReset — it is his only mobility, so a spent E is the largest cooldown in the lane. R 120/100/80 at 1000 range with an execute component.
audit.corrected: Q 10s at rank 1 (6s at rank 5), 950 range. E flat 10s, 425 range, and an auto reset — react to the wind-up. R 120s at rank 1, 1000 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] tells the reader 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal'. Soul Ignition ends by healing back a portion of the damage he took, and Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' That is a heal, so anti-heal applies; missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds does bite — it cuts the Soul Ignition refund that pays for his extended trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sequencing advice was qualitative ('the post-E window') with no durations to count.
audit.why: E's flat 10s is the same at every rank, which makes it the one cooldown a player can count reliably all game; Q's 10s-to-6s ramp explains why the nail tax gets worse as the lane goes on.
audit.corrected: Count his flat 10s E; treat every spent blink as a ten-second dive window.

notes: Three things I could not verify and therefore did not touch. (1) The page calls his Q 'Ritual Nails'; the kit file's own text says he readies 'a set of Soul Nails', and the missing-interactions file names his other four abilities (Silver Stake P, Soul Ignition W, Ashen Pursuit E, Purgatory R) but never the Q. One of those two names is wrong and I cannot tell which. (2) The page repeatedly states Locke has 125 attack range; no range for his basic attacks exists in the kit file. (3) whys[6] and the late paragraph call The Show Stopper an 'R suppress' — Riot's text for Sett's R says only that he carries an enemy and slams them, with a slow on landing, so 'suppress' is unconfirmed here as on every other Sett page. Also unverified: locke.json flags Soul Ignition with trueDamage, but Riot's text only says it damages HIM, so I made no resistance claim from it.
